messages:
amy: quick brain dump — i'm exploring collapsing region/tier predicates into a single precompiled score to reduce eval overhead in the runtime. idea is to compute a composite at compile-time for common tenant profiles and use a fast lookup during serving. pros: fewer branch checks, better cache locality. cons: staleness, less flexibility. thoughts? :thinking:

raj: i like the perf angle. two quick concerns: 1) how many distinct "tenant profiles" do we expect to precompile? explosion could kill cache. 2) how do we handle dynamic load shifts (e.g., region degradation) without recomputing everything?

amy: good Qs. target is to precompile only the top ~20 profiles (by qps) and fallback to the standard eval for the rest. for dynamic shifts i was thinking of a small dynamic delta layer applied at route-time — so we store base_score (precompiled) + delta(region_health, short_term_cost).

mike: ok but watch out for invalidation complexity. base_score + delta is fine, but delta needs TTL and versioning. if delta logic reads telemetry directly we risk amplifying noise. suggest a leaky-bucket smoothing and a 30s sticky window for deltas. also realize this adds a per-request read of a small memory table (not terrible).

claire: high-level thought: split responsibilities — compile-time for static priors (device family, region weight, tenant weight), runtime for immediate signals (AZ health, recent error spikes, capacity backpressure). keep eligibility (hard filters) separate: first filter, then lookup base_score, then apply runtime delta, then rank. keeps semantics clear.

amy: exactly. my rough pseudo: 
```
# compile step -> store in compiled_table
compiled_table[profile_id] = { base_score }

# runtime eval
if not eligible(route): reject
score = compiled_table[profile_id].base_score + runtime_delta(region, tier, recent_lat)
choose highest score
```

raj: newline: we should be explicit about when we recompute compiled_table. maybe on model/route config changes + a periodic daily recompile for cost reprioritization. also add a simple metric: percentage of requests hitting compiled path vs fallback.

mike: perf test plan: simulate 10k profiles with zipf distribution, compile top 20, measure p99 eval latency, cache hit rate. need to add cache invalidation unit tests that simulate simultaneous config churn.

claire: ops safety — if compiled_table load fails, runtime must gracefully fallback. add a healthcheck endpoint and a deploy-bot guard that prevents rollout if health unstable.

deploy-bot: canary deployed routing-compiler-v2 to staging (staging-lb-2). monitor: routing.compiler.compiled_hits, compiled_miss_rate, route_eval.lat_p99.

amy: followups/action items: 1) i'll draft RFC addendum with the compile-time format and on-disk layout + size estimates (amy). 2) raj will add sim job and metrics collection (raj). 3) mike will add cache invalidation tests and smoothing windows (mike). 4) claire will define failure modes + healthcheck semantics (claire). aim for RFC by EOW. :+1:

raj: minor nit — consider making the compiled_table iterable so we can push partial hot-swaps (stream compiles) rather than full reloads. reduces risk during rollouts.

amy: good call. incremental load sounds nicer. i'll include an API sketch for streaming updates in the RFC.

mike: small note on telemetry: keep deltas clipped to a sane range otherwise a noisy region will get extreme weight and cause oscillation. clip to [-0.5, +0.5] for starters (on normalized score).

claire: ok i'm convinced. syncing with infra tomorrow to validate memory/size numbers for the compiled_table.

amy: thanks all — i'll post the RFC addendum in #architecture when ready.
